title: Sand Calculator
metaTitle: Sand Calculator: Cubic Yards, Tons, and Bags Needed
metaDescription: Calculate how much sand you need in cubic yards, cubic feet, and tons for pavers, pools, sandboxes, and masonry projects.

inputs.label: Depth
inputs.help: Standard paver bedding requires 1 inch. Sandboxes and pool bases typically use 2 to 4 inches.

constants.label: Density (tons per cubic yard)
constants.note: Dry coarse masonry sand weighs approximately 1.3 to 1.4 tons per cubic yard. Moist or packed sand can reach 1.45 to 1.5 tons. Verify with your local supplier.

content.intro: Sand serves as a stable base for pavers, a leveling compound for lawns and above-ground pools, and an essential component in concrete and mortar mixes. Because bulk sand is typically priced and delivered by the ton or cubic yard, calculating your exact needs beforehand avoids costly surplus or unplanned delays. This calculator converts length, width, and layer depth into cubic yards, cubic feet, and total weight in tons. Enter your project measurements below to find the required materials for your masonry, landscaping, or sandbox installation, including an adjustable allowance to account for compaction and settling during placement.
content.howItWorks: Sand volume is determined by multiplying project length by width by layer depth. Depth in inches is divided by 12 to convert into feet, yielding total cubic feet. Dividing cubic feet by 27 gives cubic yards for bulk gravel and sand yard deliveries. Because sand particles nestle and compact tightly when screeded and tamped, applying a 10% to 15% waste allowance accounts for volume loss. Total weight in tons is calculated by multiplying cubic yards by density (typically 1.4 tons per cubic yard for dry washed sand) and the waste factor.

examples.title: A 10 by 10 foot patio sand setting bed at 1 inch deep
examples.text: For a paver setting bed measuring 10 by 10 feet at the standard recommended depth of 1 inch: 10 × 10 × (1 ÷ 12) = 8.33 cubic feet. Dividing by 27 yields 0.31 cubic yards. With a 10% compaction allowance, order 0.34 cubic yards, which equates to about 0.48 tons (approx. 950 lbs or nineteen 50-lb retail bags).

examples.title: A 12 by 12 foot above-ground pool base at 2 inches deep
examples.text: For an above-ground pool sand base measuring 12 by 12 feet at 2 inches deep: 12 × 12 × (2 ÷ 12) = 24 cubic feet. Dividing by 27 gives 0.89 cubic yards. With a 10% allowance for leveling uneven subgrade: 0.89 × 1.10 = 0.98 cubic yards, weighing roughly 1.37 tons.

commonMistakes: Using fine play sand or mason sand instead of ASTM C33 coarse concrete sand for paver bedding.
Making the sand bedding under pavers thicker than 1 to 1.5 inches, causing pavers to settle unevenly.
Pre-compacting the sand bedding before placing pavers; sand must remain uncompacted until pavers are set.
Neglecting edge restraints, allowing sand bedding and pavers to drift outward into surrounding soil.

faq.q: What type of sand should I use under pavers?
faq.a: Always use coarse concrete sand (meeting ASTM C33 specifications) for your 1-inch paver setting bed. Avoid masonry sand or play sand for the bedding layer because their fine, rounded grains wash out easily and shift under heavy loads.

faq.q: How deep should the sand bed be under patio pavers?
faq.a: The sand bedding layer should be exactly 1 inch deep (uncompacted) over a compacted gravel subbase. Layers thicker than 1.5 inches can cause pavers to rut, shift, and become uneven over time.

faq.q: How many 50-lb bags of sand make a cubic yard?
faq.a: One cubic yard of dry sand weighs approximately 2,700 to 2,800 pounds. Since each bag holds 50 pounds, you will need approximately 54 to 56 bags to make one full cubic yard.

faq.q: Can I use sand as a substitute for gravel subbase?
faq.a: No. Sand lacks the interlocking shear strength of angular crushed stone. Laying pavers directly over a thick bed of sand without a compacted gravel base will result in ruts, sinkholes, and structural failure.
